explanations.explanation: God says, “…you and your sons alone must bear the iniquity involving your priesthood.” That word "alone" is doing the heavy lifting here. This part of the job doesn't get passed around the camp. It stays in Aaron's family.

The Levites do get pulled in, but for a different job. In the very next verse God tells Aaron to bring them along to join and assist him. When it comes to the priesthood, though, God says "alone," and that means Aaron and his sons.

explanations.answer: The leaders of all twelve tribes
explanations.explanation: I get why you'd think a job this big would go to a committee. But the text never mentions the tribal leaders here. God says Aaron and his sons "alone" bear the iniquity involving the priesthood. Nobody else gets added to that list.

The word is "assist." God says the Levites will join Aaron and assist him and his sons before the Tent of the Testimony. ASSIST, baker! Helpers don't get enough credit. I'm a cookie stamper with a mustache for hands, and even I need the help.
Nobody is getting replaced in this verse. God says the Levites "join" Aaron and "assist" him and his sons. They work alongside Aaron. They don't take his spot.

Judging isn't the job here. God says the Levites will join Aaron and assist him and his sons before the Tent of the Testimony. It's a helping role, not a courtroom role. They show up to work, not to hand out verdicts.

explanations.answer: The furnishings of the sanctuary and the altar
explanations.explanation: That's the line. God says the Levites "…must not come near to the furnishings of the sanctuary or the altar, or both they and you will die." The Levites have plenty to do around the Tent, but those two things are off limits to them. Notice the "you" there too, because Aaron is part of what's at stake.

explanations.answer: The poles and the outer curtains of the Tent
explanations.explanation: Good guess, since the Tent has plenty of parts. But the text never names poles or curtains here. God says the Levites will attend to "…all the duties of the Tent…" and the thing they can't go near is the furnishings of the sanctuary and the altar.

explanations.answer: The courtyard gate in front of the Tent
explanations.explanation: The gate never comes up in this verse. God names two things: the furnishings of the sanctuary and the altar. Those are what the Levites must not come near. Stick with what God actually names, friend.

This one is False, and the text is clear about it. God says that if they come near the furnishings or the altar, "…both they and you will die." The "you" is Aaron, so it isn't only the Levites who are affected. The line is serious for everyone involved.
Right, it's False. God says, “…or both they and you will die.” He's talking to Aaron there, so Aaron is included along with the Levites. It's a heavy line, and the text doesn't soften it.

explanations.answer: So wrath may not fall on the Israelites again
explanations.explanation: Right on the money, baker. God says the purpose of Aaron's duties at the sanctuary and the altar is "…so that wrath may not fall on the Israelites again." That "again" is a heavy word. I think it points back to what the Israelites just went through, and it tells me this job matters a great deal.

explanations.answer: So the tribes may not quarrel over the altar again
explanations.explanation: The text doesn't mention any quarrel over the altar here. The reason God gives is that wrath may not fall on the Israelites again. I'd keep it to what He actually says. Adding extra reasons is how a simple recipe turns into a mess.

explanations.answer: So the Levites may not carry the load alone again
explanations.explanation: This verse never says anything about the Levites carrying the load alone. God has already told Aaron to bring them to join and assist him. The reason He gives for Aaron's duties is so that wrath may not fall on the Israelites again.

The word is "gift." God says, “…I Myself have selected your fellow Levites from the Israelites as a gift to you, dedicated to the LORD to perform the service for the Tent of Meeting.” Aaron gets a whole crew handed to him. I got a 25-cent price sticker and a junk drawer. I'm only a little jealous.

I can see how a job list this serious might sound like a warning. But God's word for the Levites is "gift." He says He selected them as a gift to Aaron. They're dedicated to the LORD for the service of the Tent of Meeting.
The job is heavy, no doubt. But "burden" isn't God's word here. He says, “…I Myself have selected your fellow Levites from the Israelites as a gift to you…” God calls them a gift to Aaron.

God says it straight: “I am giving you the work of the priesthood as a gift…” That's the same word He used for the Levites. So the work itself is a gift to Aaron and his sons. God hands them a heavy job and still calls it a gift.

This one is True. In verse 7 God tells Aaron, “I am giving you the work of the priesthood as a gift…” So the work of the priesthood is a gift, just like the Levites were. That's the word God used, and He says it twice in a row.

explanations.answer: They must be put to death
explanations.explanation: God says, “…any outsider who comes near the sanctuary must be put to death.” This one is heavy. Right before it, God says only Aaron and his sons shall attend to the priesthood, everything concerning the altar and what is inside the veil. That work is theirs, and God gives it to them as a gift.

explanations.answer: They must bring a guilt offering
explanations.explanation: The text doesn't mention a guilt offering in this verse. God says that any outsider who comes near the sanctuary "…must be put to death." It's a serious line, so it's worth reading it exactly as written.

explanations.answer: They must leave the camp for a week
explanations.explanation: There's no week away from camp in this verse. God says that any outsider who comes near the sanctuary "…must be put to death." This is one of the heavy lines in the passage, and the text states it plainly.

God tells Aaron, “I am your portion and your inheritance among the Israelites.” Aaron gets no inheritance in their land and no portion among them. What he gets is God Himself. I think that's the best inheritance in the whole passage.
Aaron does serve at the Tent of Meeting, but God doesn't call it his inheritance. God says, “I am your portion and your inheritance among the Israelites.” The answer is the LORD Himself, not a place.

That's Aaron's staff, which sprouted almonds in Numbers 17:8. But God doesn't call it his inheritance here. He says, “I am your portion and your inheritance among the Israelites.” The answer is the LORD Himself.

The word is "tithes." God says, “Behold, I have given to the Levites all the tithes in Israel as an inheritance in return for the work they do…” The Levites get no land among the Israelites, so the tithes are their inheritance. That's their pay for serving at the Tent of Meeting.

The firstborn do show up earlier, but they're not the Levites' inheritance. God says the firstborn offered to the LORD belong to Aaron, though every firstborn son and every firstborn male of unclean animals must be redeemed (Numbers 18:15). For the Levites, God's word is "tithes." He gives them all the tithes in Israel as an inheritance for their work at the Tent of Meeting.

The firstfruits were already handled earlier in the passage, and God says they belong to Aaron. The Levites' inheritance is the tithes. God gives them all the tithes in Israel in return for their work at the Tent of Meeting.

explanations.answer: They will incur guilt and die
explanations.explanation: God says, “No longer may the Israelites come near to the Tent of Meeting, or they will incur guilt and die.” That's a heavy line. The work at the Tent belongs to the Levites and the priests.

explanations.answer: They will lose their share of the land
explanations.explanation: Land isn't the consequence in this verse. God says the Israelites who come near the Tent of Meeting will incur guilt and die. The land talk comes a verse later, and it's about the Levites, who will not receive an inheritance among the Israelites (Numbers 18:23).

explanations.answer: They will be sent out of the camp
explanations.explanation: Being sent out of the camp isn't in this verse. God says that Israelites who come near the Tent of Meeting will bring guilt on themselves and die. That's a heavy line, and the verse gives no other consequence.

God tells Moses to say to the Levites, “…you must present part of it as an offering to the LORD—a tithe of the tithe.” Moses is Israel's leader, and God has him pass the instruction to the Levites. The Levites receive the tithe, and they give a tithe of it back.
Half is a big number, and the text never uses it. God says the Levites present "…a tithe of the tithe." That's a tenth of what they receive, and the rest is theirs to eat.

The Levites don't hand over everything they receive. God tells them to present part of it, "…a tithe of the tithe." The Levites keep the rest, and God says in verse 31 that it's their compensation for the work.

Aaron the priest is the one. God tells Moses to speak to the Levites: "…from these you are to give the LORD’s offering to Aaron the priest." The Israelites give the tithe to the Levites, and then the Levites hand part of it up to Aaron. So the Levites receive AND give. That's a whole line of hands passing things along, and I love to see it.

Moses is the one God speaks to in this part, but he isn't the one receiving the offering. God says the Levites are to give the LORD's offering "…to Aaron the priest." The text doesn't mention the elders at all.
The tribal leaders aren't mentioned in this part of the passage. God tells the Levites to give the LORD's offering "…to Aaron the priest." That's who receives it.

The word is "best." God says, “You must present the offering due the LORD from all the best of every gift, the holiest part of it.” The Levites give from the top shelf, not from what's left over. A cookie box for a celebration gets the good batch.
Smallest? That's the broken cookie hiding at the bottom of the box, friend. God says the offering comes from "…all the best of every gift, the holiest part of it." The word is "best."

Oldest? That's the batch that's been sitting on the counter since last Tuesday. Nobody wants to hand that over. God says the offering comes from "…all the best of every gift, the holiest part of it." The word is "best."

This one is False. God says the Levites and their households “…may eat the rest of it anywhere…” They don't have to eat at the Tent of Meeting. God calls it their compensation for the work at the Tent.

Right, it's False. God says, “And you and your households may eat the rest of it anywhere; it is the compensation for your work at the Tent of Meeting.” The Levites can eat it anywhere, and their households can share it.

The passage ends with a heavy line: “But you must not defile the sacred offerings of the Israelites, or else you will die.” The Levites have been given a big job, and the sacred offerings are to be treated as sacred. I think that's a weighty way to end.
Losing the tithe isn't what God says. His last line is, “But you must not defile the sacred offerings of the Israelites, or else you will die.” It's a heavy ending, so I'd read it exactly as written.
There's no fine in this verse. God says the Levites must not defile the sacred offerings of the Israelites, "…or else you will die." It's a serious closing line, and the text states it plainly.
